youtube.title: Everyone, one place | Possibility Lab No. 002
youtube.caption:
Could we fit in one city? All 8 billion, with room to breathe.

You could squeeze us tighter, but packed twice as close, a crowd starts to move like a fluid, and that's when it turns dangerous. So we keep the room, and all of humanity still covers just two or three Londons. So the world isn't full. It only feels that way from inside a city.

Series: Season 1: Impossible, worked out, part 2 of 6.

Sources
1. About 8.2 billion people were alive in mid-2024. — un.org: https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/world-population-prospects-2024
2. A crowd moves comfortably below about 2 people per square metre, i.e. about half a square metre each. — sciencealert.com: https://www.sciencealert.com/?p=28749
3. At 2 per m², everyone covers about 2.6 times Greater London's 1,572 km². — Britannica: https://www.britannica.com/place/Greater-London
4. That area is about 0.003% of Earth's land (148.9 million km²). — nationsonline.org: https://nationsonline.org/oneworld/countries_by_area.htm
5. 8.2 billion bodies at an average of 62 kg and about the density of water make about 0.5 km³: a cube about 800 m on a side, a little shorter than the 828 m Burj Khalifa. — bmcpublichealth.biomedcentral.com: https://bmcpublichealth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1471-2458-12-439
6. Across the body densities sources give (0.97–1.06 g/cm³), the cube's side changes only from about 783 m to 806 m. — biologyinsights.com: https://biologyinsights.com/do-some-people-not-float-the-science-of-buoyancy/
7. The world's tallest building (the Burj Khalifa, Dubai) is 828 m tall, the height ratified by the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) in 2010. The film shows a generic, unnamed stepped tower at that height, drawn wider than true (badged). — khl.com: https://www.khl.com/news/ctbuh-ratifies-height-of-burj-khalifa/55351.article

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Every number is checked against the sources.

Possibility Lab: Impossible questions, honest assumptions, real calculations.
